resources.string: Another equalizer app took control of the audio.
Automatic mode: if you move a band, you continue by hand from this curve
Drag or tap a band · double-tap resets it to 0 dB
This phone only allows the basic equalizer: no extra volume or balance.
This phone has no limiter: it may distort.
This phone has no limiter: here it works like “Maximum”.
Take control back if another app grabs it
Low-volume compensation (more bass and treble when the volume is low)
Each output has its own setting: your Bluetooth device, headphones and speaker. Add the “Equalizer” tile to Quick Settings to turn it on without opening the app.

Made by Carmelita Softworks. Open source (GPL-3.0).\nWinamp belongs to Nullsoft / Winamp SA. Each bundled skin is the work of its author and comes from the Internet Archive “winampskins” collection. Window positions based on Webamp.\nEqualizer design inspired by Equalizer314 (F-Droid, GPL-3.0): DynamicsProcessing on the global mix.
Without the microphone permission it can\'t measure.
Allow reading the Bluetooth device type
The curve follows the connected device, what\'s playing (music, speech or video) and the volume on its own. You can also turn it on with AUTO in the skin\'s equalizer.
Create a fixed profile for this device
It will be saved in the “%1$s” profile. You can adjust it to your taste afterwards.

1. Set the device's volume to a normal listening level (not too low, not at maximum).
2. Place the phone where you usually listen, 1–2 m from the device, with the microphone facing it.
3. Ask for silence: a “shhh” noise will play for 9 seconds.

The equalizer pauses while measuring. A phone's microphone isn't a lab instrument: the result is a good starting point, not an exact measurement.
The measurement shows how the device sounds in your room (the extremes aren\'t corrected: the microphone doesn\'t measure them well). The correction trims the peaks and gently fills the dips.

Shows the bass, mids and treble of everything that plays, live. Android asks for the microphone permission for this, but nothing is recorded. You can also add the “Spectrum” widget to your home screen.
Permission granted, but Android hasn\'t connected the service that reads what\'s playing yet. Wait a few seconds; if it stays like this, turn the access off and on again or restart the phone.
Shows what\'s playing in any app. Play some music to see it.
On the wallpaper, the skin\'s buttons control the music (tap an area without icons).
Android doesn\'t let Equalizer show notifications, so the player doesn\'t appear in the shade.

To show the title, time and pause state in the player, and to let its buttons control the music, Android requires “notification access”. The app only uses it for that: it doesn\'t read your notifications.
The spectrum over your photo on the home screen, at 60 frames per second. It uses the visualizer\'s style and colors, and stops when it isn\'t visible (with an app open or the screen off).
, requested at full resolution because the system gave less.
Set the wallpaper to see the resolution it\'s drawn at.
The chosen Winamp skin\'s window at full width, with the spectrum in its visualizer.
The full skin stacked downwards: the player, the equalizer with your bands (tap them to change them; AUTO turns on automatic mode) and the playlist with the queue of what\'s playing.
The spectrum with the skin\'s frame and colors; on top, what\'s playing and the time.
Just the spectrum, with the visualizer\'s style and colors.
This phone doesn\'t allow live wallpapers from here. Look for it in Settings › Wallpaper › Live wallpapers.
It needs the spectrum permission: first turn on “Live spectrum” above. Changes apply instantly if it\'s already set.
Only classic skins (.wsz) are supported; modern ones (.wal) aren\'t.
It isn\'t a classic Winamp skin (it has no MAIN.BMP or VISCOLOR.TXT)
This skin was imported with an older version: remove it and import it again to see what\'s playing, use its buttons and see it in full.
Classic Winamp 2 skins with their real window and original colors (VISCOLOR.TXT, MAIN.BMP, TEXT.BMP and PLEDIT.TXT). You can import your own classic skins (.wsz); they stay on your phone only.
App theme with the skin\'s colors
Like the original: 16 pixels tall; the original Winamp has 19 thick bands or 75 thin ones.
More frames per second makes the widget smoother but uses more battery. The widget pauses when the screen is off.
Paste a curve in GraphicEQ format (Equalizer APO). For example, the AutoEQ ones for your headphones.
Lowers the whole volume by as much as the highest band goes up: it never clips, but raising the bass costs volume.
The first 3 dB don\'t cost volume and half of the rest is compensated; the limiter holds the peaks.
Lowers nothing: the limiter holds the peaks. With very high bass and loud music you may hear it compressing.
Your photo with the audio spectrum animated at 60 frames per second
Real-time audio spectrum of what\'s playing on the phone

Android doesn\'t let apps link speakers from different brands: the phone\'s system or each speaker does that. Here you\'ll see the way that works with your phone and devices, and the equalizer keeps working in all of them.
You have %1$d %2$s speakers: link them with %3$s from the %4$s app. They play together, in sync.
Your phone can broadcast LE Audio: it works across brands if the speakers support Auracast. Look for it in Bluetooth settings as “Audio sharing” or “Auracast”.

Samsung lets you send sound to two Bluetooth devices of any brand: connect both and pick them in the media output of the quick panel or in Bluetooth settings. There may be a slight delay between them.
If a speaker has an AUX input, connect the other one (or the phone) to it with a cable: it works with any brand and with no delay.
No Winamp presets found in that file.
An Android effect for a wider sound, especially on headphones. Not every phone applies it to all audio.
The player with the Winamp skin, what\'s playing and its buttons
